promo-color-line-weight.title: Your coloring book lines are too thin for KDP #shorts
promo-color-line-weight.description:
Amazon publishes a minimum line thickness: three quarters of a point, or one hundredth of an inch, or three tenths of a millimetre. A coloring book is nothing but lines, so this applies to every single stroke in the book.

Canva's element line art is often half a point. It looks perfect on screen at four hundred percent zoom, and it prints as a broken dotted line — or it does not print at all. Nothing rejects the file. The customer just leaves a one-star review.

Set your own floor at one point and give yourself the margin.

▶️ Full tutorial: https://youtu.be/jyg1lX2kcUo

promo-color-scaling.title: Shrinking the art shrinks the line #shorts
promo-color-scaling.description:
This is the one that catches careful people. Take a drawing with a one point stroke, shrink it to half size, and Canva scales the stroke with it. Your one point line is now half a point — under Amazon's floor — and you never touched the stroke setting.

So the order matters. Resize the art to exactly the size it will print, THEN select it and read the stroke weight, THEN fix it. Never the other way round.

This is why a book can look flawless in Canva and print like a photocopy of a photocopy.

promo-color-bleed.title: Canva's bleed is wrong for a KDP book #shorts
promo-color-bleed.description:
Bleed on a book is not symmetrical. Amazon wants an eighth of an inch on the top, the bottom and the outer edge — and nothing on the inner edge, because that is the spine and it is glued.

So the height gains an eighth twice, which is a quarter of an inch, and the width gains an eighth only once. On an eight and a half by eleven book that is a page eight point six two five wide by eleven point two five high.

Canva does not know about spines. Its bleed sits on all four sides evenly. Do not use the bleed toggle — type the bled size in as your custom size and keep control of it yourself.

▶️ Full tutorial: https://youtu.be/jyg1lX2kcUo

promo-color-export.title: Your coloring book will print at 96 DPI #shorts
promo-color-export.description:
Canva's download menu defaults to PDF Standard, and PDF Standard is ninety six DPI. Amazon requires images at a minimum of three hundred. Ninety six is a third of what they ask for.

Choose PDF Print instead. Then two checkboxes: leave Crop marks and bleed UNTICKED, because you already built the bleed into your page size and ticking it adds a second lot on top. Tick Flatten PDF, because Amazon asks you to flatten transparency and embed your fonts, and that box does both.

One box on, one box off.
